Good morning, everybody. I call to order the meeting of the informal ad hoc working group on the mandate implementation review. This meeting is convened to take action on the draft report and draft resolution contained therein. The draft report and draft resolution contained therein have been circulated via eDelegate. Colleagues, as you know, the resolution before you reflects six months of deep discussions and consultations. Since assuming our role as co-chairs, we have engaged intensively with you, individually and collectively, to consider how we can improve our approach across the mandate lifecycle. Our consultations identified a range of priorities and perspectives on how to proceed. We have been extremely grateful for your constructive spirit and willingness to engage actively to identify common ground on the way forward. You have demonstrated a commitment to strengthening this organisation in the face of unprecedented challenges and to enhance its efficiency, effectiveness and impact for the people we serve. We approached our mandate as co-chairs to identify a set of principles and actions to improve the creation, implementation, and review of mandates by 31 March with dedication and sincerity. We also took extremely seriously our mandate to strive for consensus. In our assessment, the resolution before you represents a carefully balanced text that reflects your collective priorities, but also accommodations to acknowledge your legitimate concerns and sensitivities. We believe the resolution provides the best basis for agreement on the way forward amongst member states. Through our consultations with you, the resolution has become a tightly woven document with each element interconnected. Any changes to it would only take us further from our shared goal. All member states, minus one, have indicated to us that they can accept the final revised resolution. We know that this has required flexibility on all sides, and we're truly grateful. In our assessment, the Russian Federation's proposed amendments would unravel the delicate balance we have forged together. Most of you have expressed appreciation for the equilibrium achieved, and many of you have explicitly urged us not to reopen the text of the resolution, even if we were unable to accommodate all of your views. We take this opportunity to respectfully, once again, invite the Russian Federation to join the rest of the working group to achieve a consensus outcome. Working group members will also be aware that the Russian Federation has submitted a General Assembly draft decision seeking an extension of the working group's mandate until 30 April to continue negotiations on the text. In this regard, we must reiterate that we see no scope for any extension beyond 31 March, in line with our consistent message from the outset. It is our firm assessment that an additional month of negotiations would not produce a more balanced or widely acceptable outcome than the one before us today. In addition, neither Ambassador Wallace or I are available during the month of April. The president of the General Assembly would have to appoint co-chairs, and this is a practical impossibility in the time available. Also, as co-chairs, we are mindful that several other processes require space and tension in the coming month. It is therefore neither practical nor advisable to divert additional time to extending the negotiation process. Given we do not see any viable way for both the mandates resolution and the Russian Federation's draft decision proposing to extend the working group negotiations to coexist, We have respectfully requested the Russian Federation to withdraw its draft decision in the General Assembly. But to be clear, no action can or will be taken on the Russian Federation's draft decision today because it is a General Assembly, not informal ad hoc working group document. Colleagues, Returning to the matter of the resolution before you, we wish to emphasize our view that it represents your hard work over the past six months. The resolution provides a unique opportunity to bring us closer to the UN we want and need, one more capable of advancing our shared goals and delivering for the people we serve. We encourage you not to allow this opportunity to slip from our grasp. I now pass the floor to Ambassador Wallace.

Thank you, Ambassador Schwalger, and good morning, colleagues. Colleagues, this meeting is convened to consider the draft resolution and the draft report. The draft report, the draft resolution, and the draft amendments one to four have been circulated via eDelegate. I now give the floor to the representative of the Russian Federation to introduce draft amendments one to four.

Excellencies, dear Brian and Carolyn, I thank you for giving me the floor. I would like to use this opportunity to have a general comment and introduce my amendments. I would like to note that the main problem for the situation and the main reason for the situation we found ourselves in is the absence of negotiations. It will always be an enigma for my delegation why during the six months period there was no time to assign a proper line by line negotiations. where we could feel for and find acceptable compromises to all. You know exactly that the Russian delegation initiated the resolution on UN initiative, and when we worked out the text, we took on board 100% of red lines conveyed to us officially. We believe that the matter of reforming the UN and the matter of future of the UN requires full consensus with no qualifiers. Otherwise, we put our organization at risk by our own hands. We believe that this is the diplomacy, line by line negotiations is the diplomacy. By rejecting diplomacy, We reject the UN because diplomacy is the fundament of the UN. You mentioned that you were deciding to reopen and not to reopen. My comment is that by negotiations line by line, it will be a decision of the member states of all the delegations to reopen or not to reopen. So the ownership of the product that we have would also be 100% with the member states. That is the approach that we are commenting and we are promoting. But we are where we are. I also wanted to, whatever you might think of our delegation, I also wanted to thank you for those efforts that you have spent. I agree it is not an easy task. But our key concerns relate to the reducing the prerogatives of member states to introduce initiatives and expanding the authority of the Secretary General to mark the mandates as bad, irrelevant, or obsolete. Under the UN Charter, The Secretary General does not have that role and that function. So we do regret that during the six months we didn't find time for negotiations, but only for briefings. And some of the briefings, they were more like lectures. We are sure that all the delegations do not need lecturing, They know a lot about the UN and about mandates. What they did need was negotiations of the text line by line. You also mentioned that Russian delegation wants to unravel the balance. We do not agree with this assessment. First is that we would never have done it if we have not been approached by a number of delegations expressing concern both about the way the work was done during these six months with no negotiations and about the text on the table. Second, we do not find this text as balanced because in the long run we assign the Secretary-General with extra authorities which are not foreseen by the UN Charter and we reduce the prerogatives of the Member States to the opposite of the UN Charter. This cannot be called a balance because our delegation and other delegations were expressing these concerns since day one, and we were always transparent about these key priorities. I have to say that we tried and worked hard as well with our capital, and we downgraded our concerns to least possible concerns. I am not in a position to withdraw my proposals. I still believe that we do have a way to try to accommodate them. I am ready for engagement, but if there is no other way, then we can make a procedural decision on them now and today. I will introduce them and I want them to be considered one by one, not as a package. Amendment one is about financial obligations. We have to note that a number of countries cannot fulfill their obligations, not because they do not possess the funds, but because they are restricted with illegitimate measures which hamper their financial obligations fulfillment. We believe this problem is also impacting the mandate implementation, so it has, it deserves a place in the resolution. Amendment number two about shall to be replaced by make every effort to. We discussed at length the idea that the modalities of new way of presenting resolutions and draft decisions should take into account different capacities of delegations, different situations, and different essence of the mandates. There is no one-size-fits-all, so by putting the text as it is in your draft, might be very heavy burden for a number of delegations or can be seen as artificial obstacle for delegations when they want to express their initiative. We are sure that the UN is existing solely for the purpose of letting delegations express their views and initiatives. Sometimes it may have very big consequences and be very helpful for a lot of delegations. That's why we make it less obligatory and we want to put that the Member States should make every effort to put additional documents, roadmaps and so on and so forth, like it is expressed in paragraph two. Amendment number three. about the prerogatives of the Secretary General to review the mandates and to sign which are redundant. I thank you for your proposal to add for Member States consideration, but it doesn't address the main problem that the initiative would come from the Secretary General. although according to the UN Charter, he is not possessing that initiative. So our amendment proposal is that specific relevant UN bodies should make a choice what kind of mandates they feel is necessary for review so that they are the one who initiate the process. This amendment goes together with amending paragraph 33, subpoint seven, because it is the mandate and the scope of the future of the working group. So if we make a change in paragraph 24, we have to make a similar reflection to paragraph 33, subpoint seven, where the working group is tasked to receive and consider the proposals of the Secretary General. So it also would read that the proposal would come if it is initiated by the member states in the first place. And last but not the least, amendment number four in subparagraph G of paragraph 33 is about consensus character of the work of the working group. We would never tire to repeat that the issues like the future of the UN and the reform requires consensus. We, when we initiated our resolution, was guided by exactly this principle and it prevailed and we had a good and balanced document. I also thank you for clarifying that our draft proposal on extending the mandate of the working group is not subject to consideration today because it's a matter of the General Assembly plenary. So we think that there's still a way to correct the situation when we do not assign new prerogatives to the Secretary-General, we proposed diplomatic caveats how to deal with it and also to deal with other amendments. But we will deal with the proposal for extending the working group on Monday or on Tuesday, whatever is the schedule for the GA plenary for this issue. I thank you for your attention and I'm ready for comments and way forward. Thank you very much.
I thank the representative of the Russian Federation. I now give the floor to the representative of Norway on a point of order.

So I would urge all colleagues in this room to support the Norway motion and vote yes. Thank you.
I thank the representative of Australia. I now give the floor to the representative of the Russian Federation.

And what we achieved, let me remind you, oral briefing by co-chairs, co-chairs engagement with Nairobi, Geneva, Vienna, a meeting to hear general statements, hybrid workshops, an overall briefing. of the co-chairs summarizing feedback, another meeting of the group to hear general statements, two rounds of so-called consultation with even more general statements, but this time on a thematic topic, and closed bilateral meetings, and briefing today on the final version of the resolution, which was distributed just after the end of the briefing, previous, sorry. Thank you, Mr. Co-Chair. The present oral statement is made in the context of Rule 153 of the Rules of Procedure of the Assembly. The present statement has also been distributed to Member States via the e-delegate platform. The requests contained in paragraphs 3, 4, 6, 11, 16, 18, 19, 24, 28, 29, 30 and 33 of the draft resolution would constitute an addition to the workload for the Executive Office of the Secretary-General, the Department for General Assembly and Conference Management, the Department of Global Communications, the Department of Management, Strategy, Policy and Compliance, and the Office of Information and Communications Technology, starting in 2026. This would entail additional resource requirements net of staff assessment in the amount of $1,128,900 US dollars in 2026. 1,730,800 US dollars in 2027 and 1,625,800 dollars in 2028 and annually thereafter. Detailed cost estimates and their underlying assumptions for the requirements are provided in the annex to this statement, which has also been distributed to delegations via the eDelegate platform. Should the Assembly adopt the draft resolution, the Secretariat will, to the extent possible, seek to absorb these requirements for 2026 within the overall approved regular budget resources for 2026. In this regard, the Secretariat also wishes to inform the Working Group that its ability to implement the mandate will depend on the availability of adequate liquidity resources. Requirements for 2027 and thereafter would be presented in the proposed programme budgets for consideration by the Assembly in the applicable years. Thank you, Mr. Co-Chair.

Co-chairs, I'm honored to speak on behalf of the Pacific Islands Forum members in New York. the presence in New York. We welcome the final revision of the draft resolution and commend the co-chairs for your leadership for the genuinely conclusive process you have led. The final revision of the resolution is a balanced reflection of the working group's views and we appreciate the care the co-chairs have shown in listening to the specific needs and capacity constraints of SIDS and other small states. This resolution gives us critical opportunity to make the UN more effective, more efficient and more accountable, an outcome that is especially important for SIDS. Our delegations operate with extremely limited staff. Every new report, every negotiation and every overlapping mandate has a real impact on our ability to participate fully, Streamlining and improving mandates is therefore not just desirable, it is essential for equity and inclusivity. We particularly value the concept note, which is one of the most practical tools to emerge from this process. It brings clarity, discipline and predictability into how mandates are proposed. And as we have said many times, If SIDS, some of the smallest delegations in the U.S. system, can produce concept notes, which we already do for many of our initiatives, then it's reasonable to expect all delegations to do so. We are pleased to see the word discipline retained in OP1J. Our workload is already overwhelming. Discipline in mandate creation is one of the the few ways to reduce unnecessary burdens and ensure that even the smallest delegations can participate on equal footing. We support para 22 to 25 on review of existing mandates, especially those that request secretariat support to enable member states decision making. The secretariat is uniquely positioned to map synergies and overlaps across the mandate landscape. They simply hold information we do not. and without their support, Member States, especially small States, would spend countless hours gathering information we do not have the capacity to collect. To this end, we welcome the development of the mandate registry as a practical tool in support of Member States. Finally, we strongly support the Working Group transitioning to a new phase of work A dedicated time-bound structure is essential to ensuring that what we agree here is implemented. Without it, the benefit of this resolution will not reach those who need them most. We have heard repeatedly that existing mechanisms cannot absorb these tasks, and we agree. We need the new working group to turn commitments into action. co-chairs, improving how we create, implement and review mandate requires change in behavior from both member states and the UN Secretariat. We must all move forward together. And above all, it is vital that all member states engage constructively and in good faith to achieve consensus on this resolution. We support the adoption of the resolution and encourage other delegations to do the same. For SIDS, the stakes are high. A more efficient, effective UN is not just an institutional aspiration, it is a necessity. I thank you, co-chairs.

Thank you very much, co-chairs. I have the honor to deliver this statement on behalf of the Small States Group, which is a cross-regional grouping of small states comprising both developed and developing countries. This statement is supported and endorsed by 54 countries of the Small States Group, and the list of countries aligned with the statement will be made available after this meeting to you and to all interested delegations. Co-chairs, the SSG, Small States Group, thanks the co-chairs for their leadership in steering this process in a transparent and inclusive manner. We also appreciate the constructive engagement by many delegations on the resolution and their efforts to ensure it contains practical and effective outcomes. For small states, the final text is not perfect, but it represents an important step forward in ensuring that the UN remains fit for purpose. We are also cognizant that the text before us represents a delicate balance of interests and positions. It is important that we seize this opportunity to make progress. Allow me to make three points. Firstly, the SSG welcomes and supports the proposals in the final text as they will strengthen the UN proposals such as the concise concept note for new mandates and a comprehensive mandate registry will empower delegations of all sizes to better navigate and engage with the mandate landscape by promoting evidence and results based decision making the resolution will allow the UN to deliver greater impact on the ground request to the UN Secretary General to rationalize and understand the current landscape of reports and mandates will help inform our own further reform efforts through the continuation of the working group. Ultimately, a more effective and efficient UN will benefit all member states, particularly small delegations with limited resources. Secondly, by adopting this resolution expeditiously, we will send a clear signal that the UN and its member states can move beyond incremental adjustments and make substantive improvements in the functioning of the organization. It will also be the first milestone since the UNAT initiative began where member states are expected to showcase our reform efforts. We should not miss or delay this opportunity. Thirdly, we understand and recognize that the co-chairs have conducted extensive outreach and informal consultations. We strongly encourage the adoption of this resolution today and at the plenary next week, preferably by consensus. Given that the text represents a serious effort by the co-chairs to capture the delicate balance between the diverse perspectives within this working group, A consensus outcome would serve the important function of demonstrating the General Assembly's unity and commitment to the important issue of UN reform. It will also underscore our continued collective belief in the UN, underpinned by respect for the UN Charter and international law. Co-chairs, we look forward to adopting a high ambition and pragmatic outcome that can inspire a continuous culture of reflection and change within the UN for many years to come. We hope that all delegations will see the importance of supporting the adoption of the resolution at the meeting today and also at the meeting of the plenary of the General Assembly next week. I thank you very much for your attention.

I thank the representative of Switzerland. I give the floor to Australia.

Thank you, co-chairs, and again, thank you for your patience as we work this through this morning. First, can I add my strong voice of support for the Swiss proposal for a no action motion, and I'd encourage all member states to engage positively with that. Second, can I simply make a point which I think is an important one. Our colleague from the Russian Federation, and I again thank the Russian Federation for taking the time to articulate its concerns this morning, but I think our colleague from the Russian Federation sought to categorize what was a procedural vote this morning as a vote on the substance of the text the co-chairs have put before us. That's a surprise to me because I don't recall voting on the text at all of the resolution. and I would strongly urge all member states in this room to reflect on what we actually did this morning which was a procedural vote in relation to a particular proposal and to remind ourselves that we have yet to consider the text of the co-chairs resolution and I look forward very much to doing that so to recap I strongly support and Australia strongly supports the Swiss no action motion thank you
I thank the representative of Australia. I give the floor to Trinidad and Tobago.

Thank you, Chair. Chair, like my colleagues from Australia and Switzerland, I wish to thank the Russian Federation for bringing their concerns to the floor. And I would also like to voice support for a vote of no action on the motion before us. Thank you.
I thank the representative of Trinidad and Tobago. I give the floor to the Russian Federation.

Thank you very much for giving me the floor. I just wanted to comment to clear out things. I absolutely agree that the working group has no authority to extend its own mandate, but it is not what I'm talking about. I'm talking about a recommendation by the group to the GA to extend its working period. So there is no legal issues with that recommendation. The group is entitled to recommend it, so it's fine. And I also thank Australian delegation and His Excellency for explaining to delegations what they actually did, but I think all the delegations clearly know what they do themselves. Thank you very much.
I thank the representative of the Russian Federation. I give the floor to Belarus.

Thank you, distinguished co-chairs. For our opinion, we should use a unified approach on our decisions. So, of course, the working group cannot extend the period of time of our work, because it's the power of the General Assembly. And so regarding the resolution, it is also decision of the General Assembly, because both draft decision of the General Assembly, draft resolution of the General Assembly, and we have no power to consider resolution even today. But if we want to make a recommendation to the General Assembly, and to consider the resolution after that in the GA hall by the General Assembly. So we have enough power to make a recommendation where I think yesterday or the day before you circulated the document with the inputs of our group with empty slot for the recommendation of working group. So one of this recommendation could be to extend and we have enough power to make recommendation to the General Assembly extend the period of our work for one month. And that is why we oppose and gained motion proposed by Switzerland. Thank you.

I thank the representative of Belarus. We have heard Two representatives speak in favor of the motion and two representatives against. In accordance with rule 116, I shall now put to a recorded vote the motion by Switzerland that no action be taken on the oral proposal submitted by the Russian Federation. Those in favor of the motion, please signify. Those against and abstentions.

The Working Group is now voting on the motion by Switzerland that no action be taken on the oral proposal submitted by the Russian Federation. Voting yes indicates support to the motion by Switzerland that no action be taken on the oral proposal submitted the Russian Federation. Voting no indicates opposition to the motion by Switzerland that no action be taken on the oral proposal by the Russian Federation, in other words, to consider it. Will all delegations confirm that their votes are accurately reflected on the screen? The voting has been completed. Please lock the machine.

The result of the vote is as follows: in favour 91, against 14, abstentions 37. The motion is adopted. Since the motion for no action is adopted, the working group will not consider the oral proposal submitted by the Russian Federation. The working group will now take a decision on the draft resolution entitled Mandate Creation, Implementation and Review for an Efficient and Effective United Nations. May I take it that the working group wishes to adopt this draft resolution? I give the floor to the Russian Federation.

Your Excellency, although I pronounce this with heavy heart and a lot of text in the resolution is quite workable that we can live with, but Russia is objecting against sending such a recommendation of the document to approval by the General Assembly. We object because we take into account the procedures that we had. Thank you.
I thank the representative of the Russian Federation. I give the floor to Belarus.

Thank you. We believe that, as the co-chairs have stated, the draft decision of the UN General Assembly should be considered by the UNGA. Similarly, the UN General Assembly resolution should be also considered by the UNGA, not by the ad hoc working group. For our opinion, it is premature to decide on the adoption and considering of the resolution within the working group, because there is no consensus at all, as we all see. And we don't understand the implication of voting on the substance of the draft within the working group. I thank you.
I thank the representative of Belarus. I give the floor to the Democratic People's Republic of Korea.

Co-chairs, thank you for giving me the floor. While we appreciate your efforts as co-chairs for the last six months, we at the same time note seriously the concerns raised by a number of delegations regarding the text drafted resolution of today.

We listened carefully to.

The statement made by the Russian Federation earlier on their amendment.

We are of the view that Russian amendment deserves due consideration for the purpose of reaching full consensus among membership. That is why we voted no on motion held earlier. In this contest, we support the statement regarding the final draft resolution made by Russian Federation. Thank you for your attention.
I thank the representative of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea. I'm grateful for your patience. I give the floor to the representative of Trinidad and Tobago.

Thank you, Chair. And again, Chair, thank you very much for the patience of all delegations present. And thank you again for the hard work put in by the delegation of Trinidad and Tobago, which is to recommend that we move forward with the vote, please. Thank you.
I thank the representative of Trinidad and Tobago. I give the floor now to Norway.

Thank you. Thank you, co-chairs. I would like to second the representative of Trinidad and Tobago. It's about time we have a vote on the actual text that we have worked so hard on for six months now. So please proceed.
I thank the representative of Norway. I give the floor to Iran.

Thank you, Chair. the two rounds of voting that we had today is showing that there is no consensus or broad consensus on the issue. So we believe we need another time to reconsider the proposals made by Russian Federation. if we want to have a strong document and a strong support for the document, it's better to give the process another chance. So it's a genuine intention to contribute to the document to be accepted by the majority of the, or hopefully consensus of the committee. Thank you, Mr. Chair.
I thank the representative of Iran. I give the floor to Japan.

Thank you, co-chairs. Japan supports moving to the adoption of this draft resolution before us, put forward by co-chairs. as we think this draft documents represents the most balanced outcome of the discussion we had in the past six months. So I think extending the period of the discussion cannot bring this document to a better position. So I think now, is a time to adopt this draft resolution. Thank you.
I thank the representative of Japan. I give the floor to Australia, who will be our final speaker.

Dear co-chairs, again, I thank you for your patience and I really value the contribution by all this morning. It is important that we have a complete discussion before we proceed on these important matters, but can I just add my voice to those who've encouraged us to proceed to a vote and just for the record, I'd like to indicate that Australia will be a strong yes vote in favour of the resolution this morning, but I strongly encourage us to proceed with the vote. We know very well that we have an opportunity next week to consider these matters in the Assembly as well. Thank you.

I thank the representative of Australia. I shall now put the draft resolution to a recorded vote, as a recorded vote has been requested. We shall now begin the voting process. Those in favour? Please signify those against and abstentions.

The working group is now voting on the draft resolution entitled Mandate Creation, Implementation and Review for an Efficient and Effective United Nations. Will all delegations confirm that their votes are accurately reflected on the screen? The voting has been completed. Please lock the machine.

The result of the vote is as follows: in favour 149, against 3, abstentions 1. The draft resolution is adopted. Delegations wishing to make a statement in the explanation of vote after the vote or a general statement are invited to do so now in one intervention. I give the floor to the European Union.

Distinguished co-chairs, colleagues, I deliver this statement on behalf of the European Union and its Member States. As we gather for the final meeting of this informal ad hoc working group, I would like to express a deep appreciation to the Co-Chairs for the remarkable coordination of this process and the collaborative approach adopted in carrying out their mandate. We acknowledge your commitment to a truly inclusive Member State-led process and your efforts to maintain an open and continuous dialogue with all delegations. Throughout this long process, the European Union and its member states have consistently called for a truly transformative framework for how this organization designs, implements, and reviews its mandates. Our objective has always been the highest possible level of ambition in this regard, to enable the UN to deliver most efficiently on the ground for the people that we serve. The text we approve today contains some weakened language in some key areas, including the system-wide nature of this reform exercise, the scope of the mandate review, the request to the Secretary-General, as well as mandate retirement clauses and funding arrangements. We would have preferred a more ambitious text in that regard. However, we are conscious of the fact that this final revision reflects a delicate balance that carries the broadest possible support, as we saw also in this vote. And we believe that this final text still represents a step forward in ensuring a substantive, meaningful and potentially long-lasting improvement in the management of the whole mandate life cycle. We also stress, of course, that we do not think that more time is needed. The time schedule for our work in the Working Group has been clear from the beginning. Therefore, the European Union's member states support this outcome of the working group and stand ready to translate this resolution into tangible action. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished permanent representative of the European Union. I give the floor now to Trinidad and Tobago to be followed by Australia.

Co-chairs, I have the honour to deliver the statement on behalf of the 14 member states of the Caribbean Community, CARICOM. Co-chairs, this working group was tasked with examining how the United Nations manages its mandates across the full life cycle and with agreeing on concrete steps to strengthen that process. The outcome before us is the result of months of substantive, inclusive and transparent engagement among member states. CARICOM commends the co-chairs, the Permanent Representative of Jamaica, His Excellency Brian Wallace, and the Permanent Representative of New Zealand, Her Excellency Carolyn Schragler, for the manner in which they guided this process, which is one that afforded all delegations including small and capacity constrained ones such as ours, a genuine opportunity to contribute to the outcome. Colleagues, CARICOM recognizes the resolution as a carefully balanced outcome, one that reflects the breadth of views expressed throughout the process and the genuine efforts of all delegations to find common ground. We welcome the text as a final reflection of that collective effort, and we are satisfied that it provides a sound basis for the work ahead. We also attach importance to the follow up arrangements established by this resolution. An outcome without a credible mechanism for monitoring its implementation would not serve the purposes of this exercise. And Caricom intends to engage actively in that process. Coaches, Caricom notes with regret that it was not possible to adopt this resolution by consensus. The process that produced it was characterized by openness, good faith, and genuine partnership among delegations, and that spirit deserves to be reflected at the moment of its conclusion. We trust that the strong vote in favor of this resolution nonetheless sends a clear signal of the broad support that exists within this membership for the outcome and for the reform it represents. CARICOM looks forward to the consideration of this report by the General Assembly and remains committed to engaging constructively to secure its adoption and to give full effect to what has been agreed. I thank you co-chairs.
I thank the distinguished Permanent Representative of Trinidad and Tobago and I give the floor now to Australia followed by the Kingdom of the Netherlands and Barbados.

Thank you, co-chairs. On this occasion, I speak on behalf of Canada, Australia, and New Zealand, CANS. CANS voted in support of the final revised resolution on mandate creation, implementation, and review. The text represents a comprehensive package of important reforms across the mandate lifecycle. And it's been clear throughout this process that a vast majority of member states supported a more ambitious outcome. Nevertheless, CANS accepts the compromises embodied through the resolutions text in the spirit of collective progress, considering the important gains that have been made and in recognition of the substantial effort invested by the co-chairs and our fellow delegations in this process. CANZ sincerely thanks the co-chairs for your balanced and inclusive leadership. We commend your inclusive and constructive engagement with all delegations to deliver a carefully balanced text that will support a more efficient and effective United Nations mandate landscape while respecting member state prerogatives. Member States should now be looking forward to adopt this text as the major first outcome of the UNAT Workstream 2. We strongly urge its timely adoption in the General Assembly on Tuesday. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished Permanent Representative of Australia. I give the floor now to the Kingdom of the Netherlands.

Dear co-chairs, the Kingdom of the Netherlands, speaking on behalf of the Benelux, aligns itself with the statement of the European Union and its 27 member states. We would like to add some brief comments in our national capacities. First and foremost, the Benelux welcomes the adoption of the resolution by this working group today. We would also like to express our sincere appreciation to the co-chairs for their excellent more efficient and effective. As highlighted in the Secretary General's report, the sheer volume of resolutions, meetings and reporting requirements places a significant burden on the system. This growing workload strains the capacities of both the UN and its member states with implications for effectiveness and the quality of our engagement. If we are serious about delivering on our commitments, we must ensure that the United Nations is and remains fit for purpose. Achieving meaningful improvements is therefore not only desirable, but also necessary. We believe that periodic reflection on mandates is essential. An ever-changing world underscores the need for a more systematic and continuous approach. This is about strengthening effectiveness, not weakening the system. Although the second revision of the draft resolution does not fully reflect all of our ambitions, and we would have preferred the stronger language of the first revision, the current version still contains important positive elements that constitute necessary first steps. However, we cannot accept any further watering down of the text as it stands. In closing, the Benelux supports this resolution as it offers an important opportunity to better equip the UN system and its member states to support the people they serve. Thank you.
I thank the representative of the Kingdom of the Netherlands. I give the floor now to Barbados, followed by Syrian Arab Republic and Cuba.

Congratulations, Consul.

Thank you, co-chair. I have the honor to deliver this statement on behalf of Malta and Barbados. We join others co-chairs in congratulating you on your tireless efforts throughout this process. We commend you and your teams for the transparency, coordination, and communication that has characterized your chairmanship. This resolution sets an important precedent for the United Nations in its reform journey, and we wholeheartedly support it. We do this knowing of its implications for a number of other processes, in the UN system, including the one that Malta and Barbados have been entrusted with co-facilitating. That is the full General Assembly review of the ECOSOC and HLPF. Like you have co-chairs, we are listening closely to member states and fully appreciate the importance of aligning the ECOSOC HLPF review with, among others, this resolution and the UN 80 initiative more broadly. As impartial co-facilitators, we are looking forward to identifying, on the basis of the guidance of Member States, relevant elements of today's resolution to implement in the ECOSOC HLPF review so that we can ensure system-wide a more effective and efficient United Nations for generations to come. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished Permanent Representative of Barbados. I give the floor now to the Syrian Arab Republic, followed by Cuba and then El Salvador.

Thank you, co-chairs. Syria welcomes the adoption of the draft resolution on the UNAT initiative. Since the beginning of this process, Syria has engaged positively and in good faith in the discussions with the aim of contributing to improve the work of the United Nations and enhancing the implementation of mandate in a more efficient and transparent manner. We reaffirm the importance of respecting the exclusive role of member states in the creation and review of mandates as a key principle that preserves the intergovernmental nature of the organization. We also underline the efforts to improve the work of the United Nations should be carried out in careful and gradual manner, taking into account the different needs and priorities of member states. The adoption of this resolution marks an important step forward and provides a strong basis for continued joint work. In this regard, Syria looks forward to work closely with all Member States.

To ensure the effective implementation of this resolution and contribute to success of the process and the United Nations as well.

Thank you.
I thank the representative of the Syrian Arab Republic. I give the floor now to Cuba, followed by El Salvador and then Brazil.

Thank you. Good morning, colleagues. Cochairs, Cuba has decided to support the adoption of the draft resolution submitted within the framework of the ad hoc working group on the mandate implementation review, even though it contains some elements of concern for our delegation. We have done so with the aim of contributing positively to this process. However, we emphasize the importance of consensus in such processes. which requires exhaustive negotiation on part of the member states. In this regard, we reiterate that adopting a more conventional approach during discussions of the document involving line by line negotiations could have helped the working group reach consensus based outcomes. My delegation has emphasized on numerous occasions within the framework of the UNAD initiative that while we recognize the need for efficiency and for maximizing the impact of the United Nations, we do not favor hasty decisions, given that we are dealing with a process that proposes substantive reforms of the organization. In that regard, we believe that extending the working of the ad hoc working group with a view to reaching consensus through more traditional negotiations will allow for a much stronger commitment among the member states as we move toward the next stages of discussions regarding the UNAD initiative. In line with With the above, we believe that optimal results from the UNAD initiative will only be achieved through the sustained commitment of all member states to consensus, something that can only be achieved through transparent, inclusive, and comprehensive negotiations. We reiterate our commitment to continue actively participating in this process. I thank you.
I thank the representative of Cuba. I give the floor to El Salvador, then Brazil, Belarus, and the Russian Federation.

Thank you, dear co-chairs. Allow me, first of all, to thank you both for leading this process, as well for all your efforts to facilitate dialogue among the delegations. Thank you very much, co-chairs. For El Salvador, UN reform is essential precisely to ensure that the organization remains effective, relevant, and capable of responding to the current, but also the future challenges. In an increasingly complex international context marked by multidimensional crisis, it is crucial to strengthen multilateralism, improve the system's efficiency, and ensure that its structures and working methods are aligned with the contemporary realities. We also believe that any reform effort must preserve balance among the three pillars of the United Nations, while also safeguarding the existing mandates, institutional expertise, and technical capabilities of the entities within the system, particularly those that provide direct support to member states, especially developing countries. So effective reform must also be based on the principles of transparency, predictability and coherence, ensuring the full and meaningful participation of Member States and also maintaining their authority in decision making. In this regard, my delegation has actively participated throughout the entire process, demonstrating also a constructive commitment in good faith. And for this reason, we have voted in favor of this resolution. as it recognizes the time and effort invested by the delegations since the creation of this body, and also taking into account the need to achieve a result that fulfills the mandate entrusted to you, dear Co-Chairs, in line with the global reform efforts currently underway. Notwithstanding, my delegation will have appreciated that both the final consideration of the text and also the consultation process over the past few months had more closely followed the established practices of intergovernmental negotiations. Looking ahead, El Salvador attaches great importance to procedural approaches as well as furthering and strengthening efforts to promote timely and predictable communication that will be precisely, we hope, one of the guiding principles in the implementation of the mandate entrusted to the other working group. Dear co-chairs, thank you once again for all the efforts, for all the time, and for your leadership. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished Permanent Representative of El Salvador. I give the floor now to Brazil, followed by Belarus, Argentina, and then the Russian Federation.

Thank you very much, dear co-chairs. Before briefly commenting on Brazil's votes today, let me thank you very much for the work you have undertaken. As you know, I've been personally and actively involved in the conversations, and I could myself see the openness, the transparency, and the honesty with which you conducted this process. We voted against the first motion of no action on a principled reason basis that we believe that unless some procedural circumstances are not present, ideas should be debated by member states. We voted in favor of the second action of no motion, no action of no motion, no action, because we believe that the postponement would not lead us to further progress. The dates were quite clear from the beginning. Obviously, we voted in favour of the text because we believe that it is a sound, good text. It is not a perfect text, because there is no such thing, but it is a good text, a balanced text. And finally, again, please take into heart our heartfelt thanks for the way you conducted this process. And I think we all will be responsible for the way in which this resolution will be implemented. It's not free of risks, as you know, I've been conveying to you some of my concerns, but it will be important for us to be vigilant so that the spirit of the resolution will be fully abided by. I thank you again for all your work.
I thank the distinguished Deputy Permanent Representative of Brazil. I give the floor now to Belarus, followed by Argentina, Russian Federation, Mexico and Senegal.

Dear colleagues, as a small delegation, we understand that some of you are tired of negotiations, but seeing the group now agreed by a vote, to extend its work for a full year, it definitely had the opportunity to continue for another month. We are a small state and we were able to continue to work. Our opinion remained the same. It was premature to decide on the adoption of this non-consensual resolution within the working group. For this reason, we did not participate in the vote. I thank you.
I thank the representative of Belarus. I give the floor now to Argentina.

Thank you very much, distinguished co-chairs. Our delegation supported the working group co-chairs report, including its draft resolution. Over the past month, we have participated actively and constructively in the discussions in all their phases and formats. We have witnessed the work and genuine efforts you, your teams, and delegations have put forward to find common ground in a complex and delicate process that indeed can raise legitimate concerns and requires its own safeguards. In this regard, we understand the final version of the draft resolution strikes a delicate and necessary balance, which we take into account. We will expand our position and substantive comments during the formal adoption in the GA session. We hope this draft resolution lays the ground for a realistic and constructive work that can produce concrete results towards a more efficient and effective organization that can deliver better results on the ground and address the needs and national priorities of its member states. I thank you.
I thank the representative of Argentina. I give the floor to the Russian Federation.

Excellencies, dear co-chairs, as I said in my first statement, I still owe you a lot of thanks to the work that you have done, the way you have covered onto the stage. It's regretful that we have identified lack of consensus text. It is the situation in the world and which is reflected in the General Assembly. I wanted to first ask you to make sure that all the votings and motions are reflected in the description of the report because the report has to contain our debates and procedural motions. which is submitted to the General Assembly. I hope it is go without saying. Second, I still want to say that we have seen that a lot of delegations mentioned that it's not perfect, but I wanted to underline that Russia was not aspiring for a perfect document. I agree that there is no perfect documents in the UN. But what we aspired for was some balance between the views, and we still believe that this balance is not achieved. And we want to express our regrets that we have another document which is imposed on member states. The more imposed documents we have in the UN, the one which do not enjoy consensus, the one which were not elaborated through negotiations, the further we go from the reality. And the further UN goes from the reality is the worse for the UN. So unfortunately, I have nothing to congratulate you with. I hope that this consideration and debates that we have today will be taken into account in our future deliberations. And I thank you for your attention.
I thank the distinguished Deputy Permanent Representative of the Russian Federation. I give the floor now to Mexico, followed by Senegal and India.

Thank you, Mr. and Madam Chair. The co-facilitators have produced a final resolution on the mandate implementation review after lengthy consultation with member states. The proposal represented a step forward on a complex, interlinked, and multi-stage process on mandate review in line with objectives of UNAD initiative to attain a more modern and effective organization. Mexico expresses its sincere appreciation to the co-chairs from Jamaica and New Zealand for their dedicated efforts over the past six months in steering the consultations to bridge divergent positions across the membership on a matter of high priority for Mexico within the much needed reform of the organization. Mexico supported the text placed under silence as we believe the proposals provided a common ground for future implementation review work and it strikes a delicate balance among the diverse perspective expressed by delegations through the consultations. We believe that it is important for the process promoted under work stream two to continue advancing substantively and within the established timelines. Mexico supports the proposed extension of the group for an additional 12 months. allowing time to advance on the implementation of the mandate review in line with the objectives of the UN aid initiative, including the avoidance of duplication and the enhancement of system-wide coordination. For Mexico, the review of mandates should be carried out in a way that preserves the balance among the three pillars of the UN, peace and security, development and human rights, without any of them being overlooked and without limiting the scope of the resolution. Throughout the consultations, Mexico has emphasized the importance of calling upon the entire United Nations system to apply the principles and provisions of this resolution. Mexico reiterates that the principles set forward therein should be applicable to all UN organs, including the Security Council. Thank you very much, Mr. and Madam co-facilitators.
I thank the distinguished Deputy Permanent Representative of Mexico. I give the floor now to Senegal, followed by India, who will be our last speaker.

Thank you, dear co-chairs. Senegal aligned itself with the statement made by Singapore on behalf of a group of small states and would like to make a few remarks in its national capacity. Senegal reaffirms its firm commitment to an informed, inclusive, balanced, and fair implementation of the UNAT initiative. In this regard, the delegation of Senegal is grateful to the co-chairs for their leadership and efforts to lead this process. Similarly, Senegal welcomed the constructive engagement of delegation in drafting a text that could reflect diverse positions around the common objectives that brings us together in this informal working group. In view of the above, my delegation welcomed the adoption of this draft resolution by the informal working group even if you would have preferred for it to be adopted by consensus. Having said that, my delegation would like to emphasize three points. First, Senegal believes that this text, even if it is not perfect, represents an element on which we can continue to capitalize in order to move forward towards a United Nation that is better adapted to the current and future challenges without calling into questions the prerogative of its member states in creation, implementation, and review of mandates. Secondly, Senegal would like to reaffirm the indispensable balance between the three pillars of the Charter, which calls for the strengthening of inter-pillar efforts in creation, implementation and review processes for mandates. In this regard, the tools that the ad hoc working group will be working on must have not only the virtues of efficiency, but also of accessibility for all delegations. Thirdly, and equally important, is the fact that the effort for concession and streamlining must in no way call into question the integrity of mandates or the exclusive prerogatives of member states, which must, at the end of this process, have their decision-making capacity strengthened, thanks in particular to the better adjusted support of the Secretariat. In conclusion, the delegation of Senegal reaffirms its commitment to contribute to the implementation of workstream number two and hope that this resolution will be the first milestone toward life cycle of mandate better controlled by member state for revitalized action at the level of the UN system and with even more impact on the ground. Thank you.
I thank the representative of Senegal. I give the floor now to India.

Thank you, Mr. Kovachayath. We really appreciate your commitment to seek consensual outcome throughout this process. Our delegation engaged proactively and constructively during this process across all formats. We consider that the draft text adopted today represent a delicate balance and will facilitate the implementation of UNAT across mandating bodies. Finally, we would like to clarify that during the vote on the draft resolution, we voted in favor of this draft text and we would request for necessary correction. I thank you, Mr. Chair.

I thank the representative of India. We have heard the last speaker in explanation of vote after the vote. I now invite the Working Group to consider the draft report. Are there any comments on the draft report? I give the floor to the Russian Federation.
Thank you, Mr. Chairman, for your patience. I was just making sure that the motions will be reflected there in the voting. Thank you.

I thank the distinguished Deputy Prime Minister, representative of the Russian Federation. I see no other requests for the floor. May I take it that it is the wish of the working group to adopt the draft report and to entrust the co-chairs with its finalization in accordance with the practice of the United Nations? I hear no objection. It is so decided. Colleagues, before we conclude, allow me on behalf of Ambassador Schwalger to say thank you to all of you, every last one who has engaged in this process over the last six months. We know it has been different. It has been difficult. But we have a rare opportunity now to help to make the UN better and more relevant. And what we do with what we have in this resolution, those things that we have agreed and have adopted, is really where the determination will lie about how effective and how efficient the United Nations can become. So we urge you to continue to participate as you have, to give of yourselves to ensure that what we have agreed will become implemented over the life of the working group. We appreciate very much your patience with us as co-chairs, the thoughtfulness with which you engaged in this process, the constructive views that were brought And your facilitation in helping us to achieve a balanced text that we considered still to be of high ambition. We are grateful for your efforts along the way with us. We will see you on Tuesday at 3 p.m. here in this hall. The meeting is adjourned.
